subject: Level recommendation and comp ask for Alex Johnson — L6 vs L5
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sasha Patel <sasha@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Level recommendation and comp ask for Alex Johnson — L6 vs L5

Hi team,

Following the final interview loop for Alex (resume attached in the candidate record), the hiring manager at Acme (Sasha) is pushing to bring him in at L6 — Lead Data Scientist — because he ran the cross-team ML infra migration at his last company and has two direct IC reports. My read from interviews: strong technical breadth, some product ownership, and clear experience leading small teams, but not full org-level strategy yet.

Comp ask from candidate: $220k base, 0.5% equity target, 15k signing bonus. Acme’s budget is tight; Sasha asked if we could match the L6 band to avoid losing him. Current band guidance (Q2 lookup):
- L5 (Sr) base range: 165k–195k, equity 0.15%–0.3%
- L6 (Lead) base range: 195k–245k, equity 0.3%–0.6%

Requesting two things:
1) Formal leveling decision — do we market him as L6 or L5? Laura, your calibration notes from last quarter would be helpful here.
2) If L6, approval to offer at 210k base / 0.45% equity / 10k sign (comp package within band but above midpoint) to be competitive.

I’ve attached a draft offer packet (offer_packet_draft_v3.pdf) and the comp band lookup.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Recruiter, Talent Acquisition
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Level recommendation and comp ask for Alex Johnson — L6 vs L5

Irene — thanks for the summary and for looping me in. Quick thoughts:
- Based on the interview writeups I reviewed, Alex demonstrates clear technical leadership but his scope looks like a lead/area owner, not a strategic principal. He led a migration and managed 2 ICs; that typically maps to L5 (Senior) to lower L6 depending on depth of cross-org impact.
- My cautious preference is to position him at L5 with an elevated salary and short promotion plan to L6 after 9–12 months contingent on demonstrated cross-functional impact. That preserves our leveling integrity.

If Sasha is firm on L6 to close, we should document the stretch rationale and a clear success plan tied to promotion criteria. Also: if we offer L6, comp must be supported by Jonas’ budget/comp authority.

If you want, I can draft language for a 9-month development plan that locks expectations.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, People Operations
From: Sasha Patel <sasha@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 06 Jun 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Level recommendation and comp ask for Alex Johnson — L6 vs L5

Thanks for the transparency — wanted to add context from Acme’s side: Alex will immediately own our model serving reliability initiative and mentor two ICs; we see him as a hybrid lead/manager who will remove a major blocker. Losing him would push our roadmap by a quarter.

Willing to commit to the suggested 210k / 0.45% / 10k sign if Redwood can make the role L6 on the offer. From our perspective, title matters for retention (both internally and if he later moves). Happy to put an email here committing to the scope we discussed.

— Sasha
Sasha Patel
Head of Data Science, Acme Analytics
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 14:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Level recommendation and comp ask for Alex Johnson — L6 vs L5

Appreciate the notes. Quick comp authority check: hiring manager budget can support the 210k base within recruiting uplift allowances, but for equity 0.45% is at the upper quartile for L6 — we'll need Marissa (Comp) to sign off on exceeding midpoint. Also want to be explicit about promotion mechanics if we hire at L5 + fast-track: the budget for early promotion comes from org HC planning.

Proposal to break the difference and reduce risk:
- Offer L6 title but a conditional comp structure: 210k base, 0.35% initial equity with 0.1% backfilled as a retention grant at 9 months if promotion criteria met. Signing bonus 7.5k.
- If Laura prefers strict leveling integrity, alternative is L5 at 205k / 0.35% with a documented 9-month promotion plan.

Marissa — can you advise on whether you can approve the 0.45% or prefer the hold-and-release approach?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Engineering (Hiring Authority)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Level recommendation and comp ask for Alex Johnson — L6 vs L5

Team — after reviewing the candidate packet and market comps, I authorize the conditional-title approach Jonas proposed. Details:
- Offer title: L6 (Lead Data Scientist) to meet Acme’s requirement.
- Compensation: 210,000 USD base, 0.35% initial equity grant, retention grant 0.10% vesting at 9 months contingent on agreed milestones, signing bonus 7,500 USD.
- Documentation: recruiter to include the 9-month success plan in the offer package and a clause that ties retention grant to measurable deliverables (on-call handover, infra migration milestone, mentorship plan).

Irene, please update the offer packet accordingly and get DocuSign ready. Copy Sasha to confirm scope and timeline if you haven't already.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Total Rewards
Redwood Inference
